title: PRD: Transactional envelope for partial-streamed structured outputs and tool-call reconciliation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a deterministic, operationally-safe contract for emitting partially-complete structured objects over the streaming API while supporting transactional tool/function invocations. The goal is to reduce application-level parsing errors, make tool calls idempotent and reconcilable, and provide clear degradation modes when streams are truncated or tools fail.
background: Multiple customers have reported parser failures and duplicated tool invocations when clients reconnect to partially-streamed responses or when downstream tools time out.

Existing acceptance artifacts cover schema handshake and general streaming fallback, but lack a single spec combining streaming envelopes, sequence reconciliation, and explicit tool-call lifecycle semantics for retries and idempotency.
This ticket defines acceptance criteria for the product and engineering teams to implement a transactional envelope layer and related observability/QA tests.
goals: Define an envelope format that adds minimal overhead to streamed responses but allows deterministic reconstruction of partial objects.
Specify tool-call lifecycle (prepare/commit/abort) and idempotency tokens so duplicate invocations are detectable and safe.
Enumerate error modes and customer-visible degradation behaviors with required telemetry events for each path.
Provide a QA matrix and example test vectors for engineers and SDK teams to validate against the runtime.
non_goals: Designing a new full RPC transport — we must remain compatible with current streaming HTTP/HTTP2 SSE and chunked transfer semantics.
Mandating changes to every historical model — support must be additive via the runtime and schema negotiation headers.
requirements: Envelope: each stream message may be wrapped in a JSON 'envelope' with fields: seq (monotonic int), part_type (body|meta|tool-call|end), payload (string or JSON), checksum (optional base64). The runtime must support both envelope and legacy raw modes via Accept-Streaming-Mode header.

Partial-object reassembly: clients must be able to reassemble object state by applying envelope parts in seq order; missing seq ranges should be detectable via gap telemetry and produce an explicit 'partial' flag on the final object.

Tool-call protocol: tool-call messages must include call_id, idempotency_token, call_phase (prepare/commit/abort), and optional input_digest. Runtime must guarantee at-least-once delivery to tooling endpoints but provide deterministic detection of duplicate calls using idempotency_token and input_digest.

Timeouts and aborts: if a tool-call prepare is sent and no commit/abort is received within tool_timeout, runtime must emit tool_timeout telemetry and attach a recommended 'abort' envelope to the stream; clients must be informed via a tool_status meta message.

Fallback model variants: when a long-running tool is required and Dedicated capacity is constrained, runtime must support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant with a single, consumer-visible meta envelope indicating the fallback reason and expected fidelity impact.

Schema negotiation: client can opt-in to strict schema mode via header; in strict mode, schema deviations must cause immediate stream termination with an error envelope and non-zero exit code that is surfaced to SDKs.

Backpressure and reconnect: SDKs must be able to reconnect using last-applied-seq; runtime should support replay of buffered envelope window for up to 30s from last-seq to allow reconciling partial objects without duplication of tool-calls.

Observability: runtime must emit the following events with these fields: stream_start(stream_id, client_id, accept_mode), envelope(seq, part_type, tool_call=false), tool_event(call_id, phase, status), stream_end(stream_id, reason).
Compatibility: keep legacy behavior for simple text generation; enveloped mode must be opt-in to avoid breaking older clients.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc: A single canonical spec published to Confluence that defines the envelope JSON schema, required HTTP headers, and explicit examples for: successful partial-object stream, truncated stream with partial flag, tool-call prepare->commit, prepare->timeout->abort.
Runtime: ENG implements envelope parsing and emits the envelope events; feature flag 'envelope_streaming' controls rollout.
Tooling: Tool gateway accepts idempotency_token and rejects duplicate commit phases for the same token with 409 and stable call_id mapping in responses.
SDKs: SDKs for Node and Python expose a reconstructor that consumes envelopes and emits fully-formed objects plus meta events; reconnect helper accepts last_seq and replays buffer correctly.

End-to-end tests: Automated E2E tests (CI) cover: normal stream, truncated stream, reconnect and replay, duplicate tool-call suppression, tool timeout abort path, and fallback to model variant. All tests must pass in staging before release.

Telemetry: New metrics appear in Console: stream_partial_rate, tool_duplicate_call_rate, envelope_replay_success, stream_gap_rate. Dashboards include these and an alert if stream_gap_rate > threshold for >5m.
Migration plan: Documented rollback steps and runtime flag controls; gradual rollout with 10%->50%->100% over four cycles with monitoring checkpoints.
success_metrics: Reduce client-side parsing errors for streamed structured outputs by 95% within 8 weeks of GA.
Reduce duplicate tool invocations observed in production by 90% compared to baseline measured in the previous quarter.
Achieve envelope_replay_success >= 99.5% in staging during soak tests.
No customer-facing incidents caused by envelope mode during 30-day canary at 10% traffic.
test_cases: TC-001: Complete streamed object. Verify seq monotonicity, final object equals expected JSON, no partial flag.
TC-002: Truncated stream mid-object. Verify client sees partial=true on last object and a stream_end with reason 'truncated'.
TC-003: Tool prepare then commit. Gateway receives one prepare and one commit; SDK receives tool_call success and no duplicate commit.
TC-004: Tool prepare timeout -> abort. Gateway logs prepare, runtime emits tool_timeout, SDK receives tool_status=aborted.
TC-005: Reconnect with replay. Client reconnects with last_seq, runtime replays buffered envelopes and SDK idempotency prevents duplicate tool execution.
TC-006: Schema-strict mode violation. Server sends error envelope and terminates stream; SDK surfaces an explicit SchemaViolation exception.
open_questions: What is the maximum size of the buffered envelope window we guarantee for reconnection? (engineering suggests 30s / 1MB; product to decide.)
Should we require tools to implement idempotency_token or allow runtime-side deduplication based on input_digest?
How do we represent nested partial objects in the envelope payload without inflating per-message size? Consider delta encoding vs full payloads.
Do we need to extend existing error codes in the API to represent 'partial_stream' vs 'schema_error'?
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec + engineering spike (2 weeks) — produce Confluence spec and prototype in staging.
Phase 1: Canary (10% traffic, 2 weeks) — enable envelope_streaming feature flag for a small cohort; run soak tests.
Phase 2: Gradual rollout (10->50->100% over 6 weeks) with monitoring checkpoints and rollback gates.
Phase 3: SDK GA and docs — publish migration guide, sample code, and troubleshooting playbook.
Phase 4: Post-GA review — measure success metrics and iterate on any failure modes.
qa_notes: Coordinate with ENG and SDK owners for deterministic replay harnesses.
Create fuzz tests that intentionally drop seq messages and verify graceful partial flags.
Add chaos scenarios where tooling endpoints respond slowly or return 500s to validate abort and retry behavior.
